subject.title: iPhone Continuity Camera `--facing front` always uses rear camera

question: For macOS Continuity Camera, should `--facing` ever override an explicit iPhone camera `deviceId`, or should OpenClaw preserve `deviceId` as exact selection and surface a limitation when front selection is unavailable?
rationale: The source path shows why the report is plausible, but choosing precedence or limitation behavior can affect existing explicit-camera workflows and depends on real AVFoundation Continuity Camera behavior.

options.title: Live-repro then define contract
options.body: Use a signed macOS app and paired iPhone to determine whether front selection is possible, then either implement that path or surface a documented limitation without weakening exact `deviceId` selection.

options.title: Let facing override device id
options.body: Prioritize the user-facing `--facing` request even when a device id is supplied, accepting possible breakage for users who expect exact camera selection.

options.title: Treat as platform limitation
options.body: If Continuity Camera is confirmed rear-only through macOS APIs, document the limitation and keep the runtime selector contract unchanged.

recommendation.title: Live-repro then define contract
recommendation.body: Use a signed macOS app and paired iPhone to determine whether front selection is possible, then either implement that path or surface a documented limitation without weakening exact `deviceId` selection.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision touches macOS companion camera behavior and the node media selector contract where steipete has the strongest history.
